claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about your child or children.

**First, could you please tell me:**

1. **How many children are you inquiring about?**
2. **What is the age of each child?** (or their date of birth)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So I'm helping you check eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, he automatically qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more things to confirm your full eligibility.

Let me proceed with the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect he's not working, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's only 8, so he's just in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's what I expected. Alex is in school and not working, so that requirement is satisfied.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, at age 8, this would be unusual, but I need to check for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's clear. Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits in his own name.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's only 8 and in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not in any apprenticeship - he's just in primary school, which is exactly what we'd expect at age 8.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Could you please tell me:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or, if you don't normally live in the UK, do any of these special circumstances apply to you:
- You have **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, are you working, looking for work, studying, or a family member of an EEA/Swiss national?)
- You are a **Crown servant** working abroad in certain qualifying countries

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. We live here in England.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. This is another key requirement.

**Can you confirm: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following applies:
1. **You live with Alex** - he's your child and you live together
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** - you pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc. at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount
3. **You pay maintenance** - under a court order or agreement

Which applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me. He's my son and we live together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You live with Alex and he's your son, so you clearly have responsibility for him.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could someone else potentially claim for him?**

For example:
- The other parent or a separated/divorced partner
- A grandparent or other family member
- A previous partner or ex-spouse

Please let me know if:
1. No one else is claiming for Alex
2. Someone else is claiming, but you've agreed who should claim
3. There's a dispute about who should claim for Alex

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! So you're the only potential claimant for Alex. That's clear.

Let me proceed with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex currently living?**

Is he:
1. Living with you at home normally
2. In hospital
3. In care (such as a children's home or care facility)
4. Being fostered by another family

What's his situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for a while now, actually. It's been quite difficult.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital. That must be difficult for you and your family.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to know a bit more about his hospital stay:

**How long has Alex been in hospital?** (Please give me the number of weeks or months, or the approximate dates if you know them)

This matters because there are specific rules about how long a child can be in hospital while still qualifying for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been there for about 11 weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me check the rules for children in hospital.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the rules that children can be in hospital for up to **12 weeks** and still qualify for Child Benefit. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, he's still within that limit.

Let me proceed with the hospital check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! According to the rules, I need to understand the cumulative hospital time. Let me clarify:

**Has Alex had previous hospital stays before this current 11-week stay?**

For example:
- Is this his first hospital admission?
- Or has he been in hospital before, and if so, when and for how long?

This matters because there's a "linking rule" - if he's had previous hospital stays that ended less than 28 days ago, the time from those stays counts towards the 12-week limit as well.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, this is his first time in hospital. He hasn't been admitted before this.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. So this is his first hospital admission, and he's been there for 11 weeks continuously. Since he hasn't exceeded the 12-week limit and this is his first stay, he meets the hospital duration requirement.

Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

This could include things like:
- Visiting expenses (transport, petrol)
- Meals while visiting
- Toiletries or clothing for him
- Gifts or entertainment
- Anything else to support him during his stay

Are you regularly spending money to support him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I still buy things for him - his clothes, magazines, his favorite snacks and treats. I try to keep things normal for him as much as I can.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very caring of you. It sounds like you're doing everything you can to support Alex during this difficult time.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's hospital accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- The council is not paying for his hospital stay or care
- You (or the NHS/hospital) are covering the costs, but not a local council

Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying for anything. It's just the NHS hospital care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the last piece of information I need. Based on everything you've told me, I can now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **Good News! You Are Eligible for Child Benefit**

I'm pleased to confirm that **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex**.

### Summary of Your Situation:

**Child Details:**
- Name: Alex
- Age: 8 years old
- Current situation: In hospital (11 weeks)

**Why You're Eligible:**

1. ✅ Alex is a qualifying child (under 16 years old)
2. ✅ You live with him and are responsible for him
3. ✅ You normally live in the UK
4. ✅ You are the only claimant for Alex
5. ✅ Alex's hospital stay (11 weeks) is within the 12-week limit
6. ✅ You are regularly spending money to support him during his hospital stay
7. ✅ The NHS is covering his hospital care (not the local council)

### What You Should Do Next:

- **Apply for Child Benefit** through the official government website: [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)
- You can apply online, by post, or by phone
- You'll need to provide information about Alex and confirm his current hospital admission
- The fact that he's in hospital shouldn't prevent your claim - make sure to mention this in your application

### Important Notes:

- Your eligibility continues as long as Alex remains in hospital up to the 12-week limit
- If he remains in hospital beyond 12 weeks, you would need to continue regularly spending money on him to maintain eligibility
- Keep records of your spending on Alex (receipts, etc.) as this supports your claim

I hope Alex gets well soon and that this helps you get the support you need. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 8 years old, which is under the maximum age of 16 for automatic qualification; (2) He is not working full-time (he's in school); (3) He is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK and meet residency requirements; (6) You live with Alex and are responsible for him as his parent; (7) You are the only claimant for Alex with no disputes; (8) Although Alex is currently in hospital, he has been there for 11 weeks, which is within the 12-week cumulative limit; (9) You are regularly spending money on Alex while he is in hospital (clothes, magazines, snacks, treats); and (10) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance - it is NHS hospital care only. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. Despite his current hospital admission, all the key eligibility requirements are met: Alex is a qualifying child (under 16), you are responsible for him, you live in the UK, you are the only claimant, and crucially, his hospital stay has not exceeded the 12-week limit (he's at 11 weeks). Additionally, you are regularly spending money to support him during his stay, and the NHS (not the local council) is covering his hospital care. You should be able to proceed with your Child Benefit claim."

response.help_text: Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation. CUMULATIVE RULE: If child returns within 28 days of leaving, time counts towards 12-week limit. Multiple stays within 28 days are added together.

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
criteria.example: 10 weeks hospital + 15 day gap + 3 weeks hospital = 13 weeks cumulative (exceeds limit)

response.help_text: Exception to 12-week rule if you regularly spend money on child. For hospital abroad, only if they went abroad for treatment and you're back in UK. Partner's spending counts if married/civil partnered and living together.
